<b>Signaler une violence policière</b> <: Report police violence Give your testimony to the Ligue des droits de l’Homme (French human rights league), which records violence during protests.
Un attroupement peut être dispersé par l: A gathering can be dispersed by force after two warnings (“sommations”) go unheeded. They are announced by loudspeaker or by a signal (red flare, sound signal).
Rester volontairement dans un attroupeme: Deliberately staying in a gathering after the warnings is an offense.
<b>Si tu les entends :</b> éloigne-toi p: If you hear them: move away down a clear street, without running towards the police.
Tu dois justifier ton identité <b>par to: You must prove your identity by any means: ID card, passport, driving licence, even a witness. Carrying ID isn’t compulsory, but it avoids being held.
Sans justificatif, tu peux être retenu·e: Without proof, you can be held for checks for 4 hours maximum, with the right to have someone close informed.
<b>Droit de te taire.</b> Tu donnes ton: Right to remain silent. You give your identity and can say nothing else.
<b>Demande un·e avocat·e tout de suite</: Ask for a lawyer straight away, from the start. If you don’t know one, a duty lawyer is free.
Droit de faire prévenir un proche et ton: Right to have someone close and your employer informed, to see a doctor, to have an interpreter.
Durée : 24 heures, prolongeable une fois: Length: 24 hours, which can be extended once by 24 hours for most offences.
<b>Ne signe rien</b> que tu n’as pas lu: Don’t sign anything you haven’t read and understood. You can refuse to sign a statement.
Refuser de donner le code de déverrouill: Refusing to give your unlock code can, in some cases, be prosecuted (French Court of Cassation, 2022).
<b>Avant de partir :</b> verrouille ton: Before you go: lock your phone with a code rather than fingerprint or face, and hide notification content on the lock screen.
Pense aussi à sauvegarder tes photos ail: Also back up your photos somewhere other than the phone: it can be seized or broken.
Filmer les forces de l’ordre en interven: Filming the police on duty is legal.
Diffuser des éléments permettant d’ident: Sharing material that identifies an officer with the aim of having them harmed is an offense.
Floute les visages avant de publier, ceu: Blur faces before posting, protesters’ faces too.
Dissimuler volontairement son visage dan: Deliberately hiding your face at a protest where there is, or may be, unrest is an offense. The law allows an exception for a legitimate reason (health, for example), which you must be able to explain.
En <b>comparution immédiate</b>, tu peux: At an immediate trial (“comparution immédiate”), you can ask for time to prepare your defence. Ask for it.
Blessé·e : fais établir un <b>certificat: Injured: get a medical certificate as soon as possible, keep photos and witness statements, contact your legal team.
Victime ou témoin de violences : <a clas: Victim of or witness to violence: report it to the LDH.
Informations générales sur le droit fran: General information on French law, not legal advice. If you are arrested, the only person to talk to about the case is your lawyer.

Community Defense Map is a free, ad-free: Community Defense Map is a free, ad-free web application published by the operator of this instance (contact below). It is free software (AGPL-3.0) based on Cortège, an independent French project; the authors of Cortège do not run or endorse this service.

Permanent places (government offices, city halls, police stations, courts, hospitals, pharmacies, drinking water, surveillance cameras) also come from OpenStreetMap, updated monthly: they may be incomplete or out of date. City names in summaries come from GeoNames (CC BY 4.0); state outlines from the U.S. Census Bureau. The source code of Community Defense Map is free software (AGPL-3.0).
Community Defense Map is for protecting: Community Defense Map is for protecting each other: it maps police activity and surveillance. Reports are visible to everyone, and each person is responsible for what they post.
Not allowed: names, nicknames, physical: Not allowed: names, nicknames, physical descriptions, badge numbers, license plates, or anything else that identifies a person, whether a protester or an officer.
Not allowed: insults, threats, calls for: Not allowed: insults, threats, calls for violence or hatred, discriminatory statements.
Not allowed: false information and delib: Not allowed: false information and deliberately misleading reports.
Content that breaks these rules is remov: Content that breaks these rules is removed without notice. During an attack (a flood of fake reports), reporting can be paused or reports erased.
<b>Crowd-sourced information, not the tr: Crowd-sourced information, not the truth. Reports come from participants and are not verified unless marked “Verified by” an organization. They can be wrong, incomplete or out of date. Use your own judgment, stay with your group, and in a medical emergency or serious danger call 911.
The Rights tab gives general information: The Rights tab gives general information about U.S. law. It is not legal advice: if you are arrested, talk to a lawyer.
Community Defense Map was designed to co: Community Defense Map was designed to collect as little data as possible. No account, no cookies, no ads, no analytics. The publisher (see above) is responsible for this data.
Stays on your phone. It centers the map,: Stays on your phone. It centers the map, follows you and triggers alerts. To load reports, the phone only asks for the map areas around you, rounded to about 5 km. For live updates, it also subscribes to the large areas of about 100 km around you, with nothing kept on the server.
Used on the phone to orient your dot on: Used on the phone to orient your dot on the map.
Category, position rounded to about ten: Category, position rounded to about ten meters, optional written note, time. Visible to everyone.
Erased when they expire (10 to 90 min de: Erased when they expire (10 to 90 min depending on the type, can be extended)
When a report disappears (expired or rem: When a report disappears (expired or removed), only this is kept: category, start and end times to the minute, position rounded to about ten meters (as on the live map), number of confirmations, of “Gone” votes and of notes, and what happened to it (expired, contested, removed…); for the head and tail of a march, also their path. Never the text of notes, never a fingerprint. They are used for summaries of mobilizations: a published summary (public page and downloadable open data) keeps these points, with nothing about the people who sent them.
30 days (no limit for a published summar: 30 days (no limit for a published summary)
To limit spam, the server computes an en: To limit spam, the server computes an encrypted fingerprint (HMAC) of your IP address and of your phone’s random identifier. Neither the IP address nor the identifier is stored in the clear. The key is drawn at random for each period (6 hours for the IP address, one day for the phone), then destroyed at the end of the following period: even with a copy of the disk, past fingerprints can no longer be computed, and two days cannot be linked. Within one period, however, the server can link the actions of the same phone (one day) or the same network (6 hours).
The life of the report, and 5 minutes fo: The life of the report, and 5 minutes for rate limits
So that “Gone” votes from a brand-new id: So that “Gone” votes from a brand-new identifier don’t count, the server notes when it first saw your phone’s fingerprint (never the identifier itself). When you tap “Gone”, your phone only says whether it is within 400 m of the point: the calculation is done on the phone, your location is not sent.
26 h at most (the fingerprint changes ev: 26 h at most (the fingerprint changes every day)
For your phone’s fingerprint of the day,: For your phone’s fingerprint of the day, the server counts how many of your reports others confirmed and how many were contested. A phone that is often confirmed counts a little more. Everything resets every day, since the fingerprint changes.
To detect attacks (fake reports in serie: To detect attacks (fake reports in series, bursts of votes): event type, time and position rounded to about 1 km. The phone and network fingerprints are erased from it after one hour.
The technical address your browser provi: The technical address your browser provides for notifications, your area rounded to about 10 km, your choices (urgent announcements, dangers near you, new orders), the app’s language and the time of the last “danger” alert (so you don’t get more than one every 3 minutes). Notification content is end-to-end encrypted to your phone; it includes the public reports active around your area, so the map stays up to date without a network. Notifications go through your browser’s service (Google for Chrome and Android, Apple for Safari and iPhone, Mozilla for Firefox, Microsoft for Edge on Windows): it sees that a notification is sent to you, when, and its size, never its content.
Until you turn the setting off: Until you turn the setting off
Title, date, place, route and the note y: Title, date, place, route and the note you write, visible to everyone once approved. An anti-spam fingerprint of your phone is kept while the suggestion waits for approval.
Only for a confirmed organizer who turns: Only for a confirmed organizer who turns it on (street medic, legal team, press, head or tail of a march): the phone’s position is sent every 30 seconds and shown on the map with the organizer’s name, rounded to about ten meters. The server keeps only the last position, plus, for the head and tail of a march only, the path of the last 30 minutes. Sharing stops by hand, at the end of the chosen duration, after 4 hours at most, without a confirmation every 30 minutes, or as soon as the phone moves more than 2 km from its starting point (and from the march route): that distant position is never recorded. The starting point is only used for this check and is never published.
State, city, dates, measures and the sou: State, city, dates, measures and the source link you send, visible to everyone once approved by the admin. An anti-spam fingerprint of your phone is kept with the suggestion.
The name and number of the person to ale: The name and number of the person to alert stay on your phone. The text message is sent from your phone, on your plan: it does not go through Community Defense Map.
What you type goes through the Community: What you type goes through the Community Defense Map server, then to OpenStreetMap’s search service (Nominatim), without your IP address.
Random anti-spam identifier, your own re: Random anti-spam identifier, your own reports (so you can extend or correct them), hidden announcements, map pieces already shown, reports waiting for a network, settings (language, battery saver, voice alert, places shown, calendar hidden on the map), meeting point, notification area and choices, the last state of the map and the last reports received by notification (to show them without a network), SOS contact, the access link for organizations and, on the admin’s phone, the admin key.
Until you clear the site’s data: Until you clear the site’s data
To be able to correct abuse, organizer a: To be able to correct abuse, organizer actions (verification, removal, announcement, event) are recorded with the time, the organizer’s name, the report type, a position rounded to about 100 m and, for an announcement or a corrected note, its text and the published number. No IP address. A removed point can be restored for one hour: during that time it is kept in full, with the anti-abuse fingerprints of the people who reported or confirmed it. For organizers invited by another organizer, the sponsoring organizer also sees their latest actions.
